title: Iran says it destroyed a US radar in Bahrain; US Central Command says it shot down two drones
dek: The first Iranian drone attack on a Gulf country since early September came during a fragile lull. The two sides give opposite accounts of the result.
what: On Saturday, 14 November 2026, Iran's Revolutionary Guard (IRGC) launched two one-way attack drones toward Bahrain, according to US Central Command (CENTCOM). CENTCOM said, as quoted by The Tribune (India): "The IRGC launched two one-way attack drones toward Bahrain and both were shot down by U.S. forces. There were no injuries or damage."

The IRGC Aerospace Force said it destroyed a US early-warning radar installation in Bahrain. The Tribune reports the IRGC called it retaliation for a US air strike on a telecommunications tower in Iran's Sirik area, about an hour earlier, and a warning that it is "on full alert to respond without limits" if the US repeats it. I did not find a US account of a strike on that tower.

The Nation (Pakistan) reports this was the first Iranian attack on a Gulf country since early September, in what it calls a fragile lull in a conflict that began on 28 February 2026. Bahrain hosts the headquarters of the US Navy's Fifth Fleet.
The claims do not match. The IRGC says the radar was destroyed. CENTCOM says nothing was damaged. I found no independent report of damage in Bahrain, and I could not check either side's claim myself.
Early posts on X called it an attack "right now" on Bahrain. One of them added that its author assumed the drones were intercepted; that was a guess when posted and CENTCOM later said so.
why: Iran, the US and Gulf states are in a long conflict, and any break in the lull moves oil and flights and gets read for what comes next.
common: On the record: CENTCOM says two IRGC drones were launched toward Bahrain and shot down with no injuries or damage. The IRGC says it destroyed a radar. Established by both sides: the drones were launched. Not established: any damage, and any US strike on the Sirik tower. Those rest on one side's word.
next: Whether independent imagery or reporting shows damage in Bahrain, and whether the US or Iran acts again.
